text.p: Adam Graves scored twice, including the game-tying goal midway through the third period, as the New York Rangers and Boston Bruins played to a 4-4 tie on Saturday.
With Boston leading 2-1 and Niklas Sundstrom serving a minor penalty, Graves wristed a shot past Boston's Bill Ranford's stick side at 9:21 of the second period, tying the game.
All-time NHL scoring leader Wayne Gretzky, playing in his first game as a Ranger, did not score.

In Hartford, Sean Burke stopped 30 shots for his 11th career shutout and Alexander Godynuk scored the only goal of the game early in the second period to give the Hartford Whalers a 1-0 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes in the season opener for both teams.
Burke turned aside nine shots in the first period, 12 in the second and nine in the third.
He made a pad save on Dallas Drake's partial breakaway with 2:58 remaining to preserve the shutout.
The Coyotes, who moved to Phoenix over the summer following 17 years as the Winnipeg Jets, lost their debut under new coach Don Hay.

In Pittsburgh, Shawn Burr's goal 97 seconds into overtime capped a wild finish as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins 4-3, ruining a 39-save performance by goaltender Tom Barrasso.
John Cullen stole the puck from a Pittsburgh defenceman in the neutral zone and skated into the Penguins zone with Burr and he scored.
At New Jersey, Brian Rolston and Steve Thomas scored second-period goals and the New Jersey Devils held off the Detroit Red Wings 3-1 in the season opener for both teams.

The Devils swept the Red Wings in four games in the 1994-95 Stanley Cup Finals and opened 1995-96 campaign with four straight wins but became the first defending champion in 26 years to fail to make the playoffs the following season.

In Philadelphia, John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 31 shots and Bill Lindsay set up a pair of goals as the Florida Panthers opened defence of their Eastern Conference title with a 3-1 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers.

The defending Atlantic Conference champion Flyers were stunned, four games to two, by the Panthers in last seasons' conference semifinals. Philadelphia, playing their first game in the new CoreStates Centre, was without superstar centre Eric Lindros, who missed the game with a groin injury.

In Washington, Sergei Krivokrasov, Eric Weinrich and James Black all scored second-period goals and Ed Belfour made 21 saves, leading the Chicago Blackhawks to a 5-2 win over the Washington Capitals in the season opener for both clubs.
After a scoreless first period, Chicago scored on a power play. With Keith Jones off for holding, Krivokrasov snapped a shot past Washington goaltender Jim Carey.
In Montreal, Alexei Yashin scored on a rebound midway through the third period to lift the Ottawa Senators into a 3-3 tie with the Montreal Canadiens in the season opener for both teams.
"I guess I can take credit for it, but it was a lucky shot," Yashin said. "I was in the right place at the right time. I'm happy to be able to help my team. I can see the Senators are a better team."
Each team had one shot on goal in the overtime with neither getting a quality scoring chance.

In Toronto, Mike Craig and Dave Ellett scored first-period goals and Felix Potvin made them stand up as the Toronto Maple Leafs defeated the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 4-1 in the season opener for both teams.
Kirk Muller had a goal and an assist and Mathieu Schneider added a pair of assists for the Maple Leafs, who gave Mike Murphy a win in his debut as coach.
In Dallas, Craig Ludwig and Pat Verbeek scored 18 seconds apart in the third period to erase a one-goal deficit the Dallas Stars defeated the Colorado Avalanche 4-1.
Greg Adams added a pair of scores in the final 12 minutes for Dallas, which got 28 saves from Andy Moog. Mike Modano added a pair of assists on the final two tallies for the Stars.
In San Jose, Bernie Nicholls scored with 14 seconds left in the third period to lift the San Jose Sharks into a 2-2 tie with the New York Islanders.

Trailing 2-1 with just under a minute left in the third period, San Jose pulled goaltender Chris Terrerri for an extra attacker. Nicholls took a pass from Owen Nolan and was just inside the right circle as he blasted a slap shot past goalie Tommy Salo.
In Vancouver, Alexander Mogilny and Esa Tikkanen scored first-period goals and Kirk McLean stopped 28 shots as the Vancouver Canucks beat the Calgary Flames 3-1 in the season opener for both teams.
Mogilny -- a 55-goal scorer last season -- took a pass from Trevor Linden, came in on a breakaway and scored off past Calgary goaltender Trevor Kidd off the left post.
